episodes.162046: Showers and thunderstorms erupted across the Tennessee Valley on October 6th, repeatedly moving across Marshall County, which caused widespread flash flooding. Numerous roadways were washed out across Arab, and sadly, 2 fatalities occurred during this flood event (one of which was a child swept away in a vehicle).
episodes.162047: Showers and thunderstorms developed across Northwest Alabama, repeatedly moving across portions of Lauderdale, Colbert, and Limestone Counties. Flash flooding occurred on the 5th, with several roadways impacted by the floodwaters.
episodes.162462: A large upper level low positioned west of the region along with an inverted trough positioned near the southern edge of high pressure offshore set up an environment favorable for strong to severe thunderstorms across coastal waters.
episodes.162957: A very moist and marginally unstable airmass ahead of a deep upper-level low over the lower Mississippi Valley resulted one report of a tree down and several flash flooding reports over middle Georgia. Heavy rainfall amounts of 1.5 to 3 inches were observed along a line from Thomaston to Gray to Eatonton to Comer, with pockets of higher amounts between 4 and 8 inches.
episodes.163230: A cold front moved through the region during the Oct 6-7 period with thunderstorms along the coast bringing gusty winds in excess of 34 knots to some areas.
episodes.163301: Central Kentucky was located in the warm sector ahead of a surface low to the west, a west to east oriented warm front to the north, and a north to south oriented cold front to the southwest. Moderate instability and shear from strong southern flow took advantage of the added Gulf of Mexico moisture. This produced thunderstorms that caused isolated severe wind damage and flash flooding over the two day period.
episodes.163562: Showers and storms developed in an unstable airmass in the vicinity of an upper level low pressure system. Hail was the primary hazard with these storms but flooding also occurred thanks to the moisture in place across the region.
episodes.163568: A deep 500 MB low over the lower Mississippi Valley, and associated surface low that was nearly stationary beneath it, produced a humid tropical air mass over the area. Convection anchored over the southern Plateau and produced flash flooding in areas that flooded just a few weeks earlier.
episodes.163569: An upper-level low just off the southern California Coast moved across The Southwest with steady rain. As the wave moved across Arizona, the abnormally cold air mass aloft and daytime heating allowed a few strong to severe thunderstorms to form.
episodes.163576: An upper level trough just west of the Mississippi River on October 3rd become stationary and evolved into a closed upper low by October 5th. The closed upper low remained nearly stationary for 48 hours and before finally lifting northward on October 7th. This system brought a variety of severe weather across Central Alabama over a five day period, including wind damage, large hail and extensive flash flooding. The most impactful flooding taking place during the evening of October 6th. Torrential, training rain and thunderstorms produced excessive rain totals across Blount, Shelby and Jefferson Counties and resulted in two fatalities in Shelby County.
episodes.163712: Locally heavy rain well ahead of low pressure over the Tennessee Valley led to an instance of flooding.
episodes.163785: The combination of a stalled front and very slow moving upper level low combined with very deep Gulf moisture to generate rounds of showers and thunderstorms. Rainfall amounts of 4 to 12 inches fell across the area and led to numerous reports of flooding. Significant flash flooding was reported in parts of Escambia County AL, particularly from Brewton east to the Damascus area. The Murder Creek in Brewton crested in moderate flood stage at just under 27 feet on the morning of October 6th.
episodes.163855: Scattered thunderstorms moved northeast across southeast Arizona and produced strong wind gusts and marginally large hail.
episodes.163898: A storm system brought flash flooding and high winds to portions of southern Utah and severe thunderstorm wind gusts to portions of northern Utah.
episodes.163998: Scattered showers and thunderstorms developed across Middle Tennessee during the afternoon hours on October 5. There were a few reports of flooding across the area.
episodes.163999: Scattered showers and thunderstorms developed in the afternoon hours on October 6th and lasted well into the evening hours. Multiple reports of damaging winds, flash flooding, some hail, and even a tornado were received.
episodes.164042: As the region transitioned out of the monsoon, a compact low created a high shear - modest CAPE environment. Parameters were sufficient for supercell development and a few supercells did develop amongst isolated to scattered storms in the afternoon across South-central Arizona, including a right-mover that pushed into Phoenix and a left split. The environment was supportive of severe to large hail with lower freezing levels and steep mid-level lapse rates. Measured hail stones up to 1.0 to 1.5 diameter was observed with the few supercells. Most other storms also produced smaller hail throughout the day. Damaging winds and isolated flash flooding was also observed through the afternoon.

Numerous trees were also snapped and uprooted in all directions and power lines blown down. Path length 0.99 miles and path width 50 yards. Max winds 90 mph.
